newsitem.title: UK: First IPE natural gas contract rolls in thin market. [CORRECTED 19:52 GMT]
newsitem.headline: First IPE natural gas contract rolls in thin market. [CORRECTED 19:52 GMT]

text.p: IPE natural gas futures closed higher again on Thursday as front month March rolled, the first monthly contract to reach completion.
The last March deal was done at 10.15 pence a therm, up by 0.15 pence from Wednesday's close but well down from the contract high of 14.90 pence.
And only 80 lots traded, of which 55 were done in March. This disappointed some players who had hoped to see higher volumes done on the last day as participants looked to close out positions.
"We saw some reasonable volumes in the last couple of days," said a broker. "If anyone was getting out of a position, then they did it in the last couple of days and not today."

He added that trade had been "frustrating" as there were good bids and offers in a tight range but they still did not result in trade getting done. "People have erred on the side of caution," he said.
But some were encouraged that the contract saw its first Exchange For Physical (EFP) done on Thursday afternoon, at 200 lots for March.
(Correction removes reference to March open interest).
Apart from March, trade was extremely thin, with two deals each in April and July and just one in August. The prices were slightly firmer in each case.
